questions.prompt: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
options: They are interchangeable words for successful password comparison.
A valid token automatically grants every administrative permission.
Authorization should be performed only in frontend components.
Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization decides whether that caller may perform this action on this resource.
questions.answer_key: Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization decides whether that caller may perform this action on this resource.
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization decides whether that caller may perform this action on this resource. This is especially relevant to “Token-Based Authentication” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Token-Based Authentication”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Test a valid identity with and without permission for the requested action.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Test a valid identity with and without permission for the requested action.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Token-Based Authentication”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Login success is treated as permission to access every resource.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: Login success is treated as permission to access every resource.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
